title: Risk Sentiment
headline_read: Markets are calm — volatility and credit stress are low.

indicators.title: Volatility · VIX
indicators.context: The market's 'fear gauge' — the expected volatility of the S&P 500 over the coming month. It spikes when investors are scared and falls when calm.
indicators.read: The VIX is at 18.5 — markets are calm.

indicators.title: High-Yield Credit Spread
indicators.context: The extra yield investors demand to hold risky 'junk' corporate bonds over Treasuries. It widens when markets fear defaults — an early stress signal.
indicators.read: The high-yield spread is 3.45% — tight, signaling calm credit conditions.

indicators.title: Investment-Grade Credit Spread
indicators.context: The same risk premium for higher-quality corporate bonds. Because these borrowers are safer, widening here signals stress reaching the core of credit.
indicators.read: The investment-grade spread is 1.25% — tight, signaling calm credit conditions.

indicators.title: Financial Conditions · NFCI
indicators.context: The Chicago Fed's broad gauge of financial conditions across money, debt, and equity markets. Zero is average; positive means tighter (more stressed) than normal.
indicators.read: The NFCI is -0.38 — financial conditions are looser than average.
